notes:
The single most consequential thing in this chunk follows directly from the researcher's one-line objection at 2026-08-13T22:09:32 ("Why are we trying to measure the noise? Let's fix the issue that's coming up, or first find it"). Claude was about to spend GPU measuring a noise floor; the researcher refused, and the hunt found that the noise was not noise — every diagnostic in the file drew from the same global `random` generator that `build_stream()` uses to choose segment lengths, and the stream is rebuilt every epoch, so two runs with the same seed, code and corpus that differed only in HOW MUCH THEY MEASURED trained on different text. Five distinct leaks (eval-time expert exploration, chaining-path utilization recording, the timing probe's `.backward()` reaching world-model params via the `WORLD_FEEDBACK` monkey-patch, halt_ema/_mass_ema averaging eval passes into a "during TRAINING" figure, and direct probe draws) plus a per-(SEED, epoch) stream generator. Commit c76dc74.

The second-most consequential is the researcher's persistent objection at 18:24 / 19:20 / 19:41 that the seeds were building off each other. The hypothesis itself was wrong — settled definitively when the researcher ran the seeds in order 2, 0, 1 and got numbers identical to three decimals — but pressing it produced a 39-channel audit that found one real bug, forced the RESUME/tokenizer-pairing hazard into the open, and led directly to the researcher's reframe ("we can utilize this for our system, building off of it (intentionally)... it is a helpful lever"), which unblocked the project's first-ever continual-learning run that same evening: eng HELD at +0.052 ± 0.075 while Python was learned from scratch to 2.276.

Two results in this chunk are the project's best on record and both came from turning something OFF: FAB_GROW=0 gave 1.989 b/B (previous best 2.140) and cut the seed spread from 2.074 to 0.326.

Caution for synthesis: the ordering of retractions matters here. "Restarts are net-negative" was retracted, then its replacement ("restarts help by 0.922") was itself framed as inside noise, and then the noise figure it was judged against was itself retracted as stale. Very little quantitative claim from before commit c76dc74 survives, and Claude says so explicitly: "no number in the record predates these fixes safely."

Container rollbacks to 2c705c7 occurred at least four more times in this chunk (00:02, 12:15, 18:16, 21:02), each wiping the working tree, levers.py/vocab.py/runs.py and the scratchpad. Nothing was lost — everything was on origin — but one of them caused a false retraction (the "smoke was never committed" episode) because `git log --all` was run against a reverted `.git`.

No sources were unreadable; the full file was read.
